behavior_problem_candidates.assessment: The direct, already-published match: history is represented as ordered semantic IDs and a generative model predicts the next item's semantic ID; the item codebook is learned in hyperbolic space.
behavior_problem_candidates.candidate: Hyperbolic semantic-ID generation for next-item prediction from chronological user interaction histories

behavior_problem_candidates.assessment: The inspected HypRQ-VAE full text generates codes from item textual features and then conditions next-item generation on histories. It discusses collaborative semantics and compares against methods incorporating them, but its described ID encoder is text-feature based. A distinct behavior-first or interaction-conditioned hyperbolic code assignment is therefore a plausible follow-up, not a demonstrated result of that paper.
behavior_problem_candidates.candidate: Behavior-aware collaborative signals in hyperbolic semantic-ID assignment, beyond item-text quantization

behavior_problem_candidates.assessment: Established neighboring problem family, but these records do not support claims about semantic-ID generation.
behavior_problem_candidates.candidate: Hyperbolic sequential behavior modeling without generative semantic IDs

limitations: The direct triple-overlap result is HypRQ-VAE (arXiv:2609.03369v1); it was independently checked against public arXiv full text. Other papers are included only as clearly labeled adjacent evidence, not as triple-overlap claims.

The HypRQ-VAE record is a 2026 arXiv preprint (v1), despite arXiv's page/comment metadata reporting acceptance for ICDM 2026; distinguish preprint availability from final proceedings publication and verify final bibliographic metadata separately before citation.

The HypRQ-VAE paper evaluates standard sequential/generative recommendation benchmarks and reports gains, especially for tail items; this is evidence about its reported experiments, not independent replication or proof of deployment impact.
The exact triple-overlap literature appears extremely sparse in the verified sample. Do not infer that no other work exists or repeat the paper's priority claim without a systematic database search.
ABSTRACT labels mean only the public abstract was used to establish the adjacent claim. No unseen future/test interactions, prompts, or datasets were accessed or inferred.

sources.exact_overlap: Directly addresses all three dimensions: sequential user behavior / next-item prediction, hyperbolic geometry, and generated semantic IDs. The full text says in III-C that chronological interaction-history semantic IDs are input and the next item's semantic ID is generated autoregressively; III-B defines the semantic ID as residual-quantization code indices in hyperbolic space. The abstract and experiments explicitly concern generative recommendation and long-tail items.
sources.independently_verifiable_basis: Public arXiv HTML full text was inspected, including sections III-B and III-C; arXiv page identifies version/date and links the PDF. DOI is the arXiv/DataCite DOI.
sources.notes: Current as of the frozen run date; arXiv v1 posted 2026-09-03. The paper itself claims this is the first hyperbolic item-indexing framework for generative recommendation; treat that as an author claim, not an independently established priority fact.
sources.title: HypRQ-VAE: Hyperbolic Item Indexing for Long-Tail-Aware Generative Recommender Systems

sources.exact_overlap: Supports the behavior-plus-generative-semantic-ID intersection: the abstract and full text describe a Transformer sequence-to-sequence model predicting the next item a user interacts with from a session, using semantically meaningful tuples of codewords (Semantic IDs). It does not use hyperbolic geometry; it is the Euclidean/generative-retrieval baseline rather than a full three-way overlap.
sources.independently_verifiable_basis: Public arXiv abstract page and linked full-text HTML/PDF; version 3 lists NeurIPS 2023 acceptance.
